objective: Verify that a signed-in Organization user is offered the six modules named in ETA-411, can open them from the Dashboard icons and from the top-right navigation menu, can reach Organization and Vault grouped beneath Preferences, and can return to the Home page using Command Center - and that a visitor who is not signed in is refused a module and kept on the sign-in page. Each scenario asserts only what its approved acceptance criterion asserts.

inScope: Presence of the six named modules Home, New Transaction, Workspace, Preferences, Organization and Vault (AC-ETA-411-001).
Opening New Transaction, Workspace and Preferences from the Dashboard icons (AC-ETA-411-003).
Opening Home, New Transaction and Workspace from the top-right navigation menu (AC-ETA-411-004).
Preferences being offered in the navigation menu with Organization and Vault grouped beneath it, as a presence check only (AC-ETA-411-005).
Opening Organization and Vault from beneath Preferences (AC-ETA-411-006).
Returning to the Home page from each module using Command Center (AC-ETA-411-007).
An unauthenticated visitor requesting a module being shown an error and kept on the sign-in page (AC-ETA-411-009).
outOfScope: The absence half of REQ-ETA-411-001 - that no module outside the organization's authorized set is offered. AC-ETA-411-002 carries that claim and is DEFERRED, so REQ-ETA-411-001 is only partially covered by this plan. The test account can reach nineteen navigable destinations while the story names six; verifying six are present says nothing about whether the other thirteen should have been hidden.

Consistency between the UI and any supporting API (REQ-ETA-411-006 / AC-ETA-411-008). Deferred by the owner, and doubly blocked: walked evidence records all six destinations as full document requests, and anything captured by observation is OBSERVED and may never judge an acceptance criterion.

Refusal of an authenticated but unauthorized user (AC-ETA-411-010). With scope narrowed to the six modules this account is authorized for, no unauthorized module remains to request, so the scenario cannot be produced at all this release.
Asserting the exact wording of the unauthenticated error message. The text is captured at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION as OBSERVED and may only be asserted if a human approves that string at this gate.
The behaviour of the thirteen navigable destinations that ETA-411 does not name, including the analytics and Vault Content entries.

assumptions: The configured eCore account is an Organization account authorized for all six named modules. Every positive scenario depends on this; if the account loses an authorization, those scenarios fail for an environment reason rather than a product defect.

Preferences is a group heading over Organization and Vault rather than a destination of its own in the navigation menu. This is the owner's answer recorded in AMB-ETA-411-007 and is why AC-ETA-411-005 is a presence check. The Dashboard Preferences icon is separate and does navigate.
The six modules are reachable in a single browser session; no scenario needs a second organization or a second account.
dependencies: requirements/approved/ETA-411.json - the approved acceptance criteria this plan may cover.
reports/validation/ETA-411-navigation-validation.json - walked evidence that each Dashboard icon reaches its destination, and that Command Center returns Home.
reports/validation/ETA-411-home-icons-probe.json - structural observation of the Home page icons and the navigation menu entries.
A configured ECORE_* organization credential in the local .env, read only through env.requireEcoreLogin().

risks.description: Organization in the navigation menu and the Preferences icon on the Dashboard resolve to the same destination, /ssweb/setup/prefs/preferences.eo. A scenario that asserts arrival by destination alone would pass while showing the wrong page, and would keep passing if the two were ever wrongly wired together.
risks.mitigation: TS-ETA-411-005 asserts arrival on page content rather than on destination. The same constraint is recorded in the rationale of AC-ETA-411-006 so it survives into automation design.

risks.description: The Command Center control is a background-image div with no text, no accessible name and no title, so it cannot be reached by any preferred accessible locator.
risks.mitigation: TS-ETA-411-006 depends on it, and the automation will need a VALIDATED waiver under SEM-AUTOMATION-HYGIENE. If the missing accessible name is itself judged a defect, that is a separate finding and not something this plan may decide.

risks.description: New Transaction and Workspace each appear twice on the Home page - once as a Dashboard icon and once in the navigation menu - so an unscoped locator matches two elements and fails Playwright strict mode.
risks.mitigation: TS-ETA-411-002 and TS-ETA-411-003 are deliberately separate scenarios by entry point, so each one scopes to a single container instead of disambiguating by position.

risks.description: This plan can produce a full pass while REQ-ETA-411-001, REQ-ETA-411-006 and REQ-ETA-411-007 remain only partly covered, which invites the coverage figure to be read as completeness.
risks.mitigation: AC-ETA-411-002, -008 and -010 stay in the requirement artifact as DEFERRED and are never mapped to a scenario here, so the RTM reports those requirements as partial rather than met.

risks.description: The unauthenticated scenario could drift into asserting whatever error text the application currently emits, which would make today's behaviour the definition of correct and would hide a regression to a different wrong message.
risks.mitigation: TS-ETA-411-007 asserts that an error message is present and that the sign-in page is still displayed. The captured string is presented at this gate; only an approved string may be asserted, and only in a later plan version.

scenarios.title: The six named modules are offered to a signed-in Organization user
preconditions: An Organization user is signed in to eCore.
steps: View the modules offered on the Home page.
Open the top-right navigation menu and view the modules offered there.
scenarios.expectedResult: Home, New Transaction, Workspace, Preferences, Organization and Vault are each offered to the user. This scenario covers presence only; that each one opens is carried by TS-ETA-411-002, TS-ETA-411-003 and TS-ETA-411-005.
testDataRequirements: The configured Organization account, read only through env.requireEcoreLogin().

scenarios.title: The Dashboard icons open New Transaction, Workspace and Preferences
preconditions: An Organization user is signed in to eCore.
steps: Select the New Transaction icon on the Dashboard and confirm its module is shown.
Select the Workspace icon on the Dashboard and confirm its module is shown.
Select the Preferences icon on the Dashboard and confirm its module is shown.
scenarios.expectedResult: Each of the three Dashboard icons opens its own module. Arrival is judged on the content of the page reached, not on the address alone.
testDataRequirements: The configured Organization account, read only through env.requireEcoreLogin().

scenarios.title: The navigation menu opens Home, New Transaction and Workspace
preconditions: An Organization user is signed in to eCore.
steps: Open the top-right navigation menu and select New Transaction, then confirm its module is shown.
Open the navigation menu again and select Workspace, then confirm its module is shown.
Open the navigation menu again and select Home, then confirm the Home page is shown.
scenarios.expectedResult: Each of the three menu entries opens its own module. Kept separate from TS-ETA-411-002 because New Transaction and Workspace appear in both the Dashboard and the menu, and each entry point deserves its own evidence.
testDataRequirements: The configured Organization account, read only through env.requireEcoreLogin().

scenarios.title: Preferences is offered in the navigation menu with Organization and Vault grouped beneath it
preconditions: An Organization user is signed in to eCore.
steps: View the Preferences entry and the entries grouped beneath it.
scenarios.expectedResult: Preferences is offered in the menu, and Organization and Vault are grouped beneath it. A presence check by design: the owner confirmed Preferences is a heading over those two entries, so asserting that it opens a page of its own would go beyond both the story and the evidence.
testDataRequirements: The configured Organization account, read only through env.requireEcoreLogin().

scenarios.title: Organization and Vault open their own pages from beneath Preferences
preconditions: An Organization user is signed in to eCore.
steps: Open the top-right navigation menu and select Organization beneath Preferences, then confirm the Organization page is shown.
Open the navigation menu again and select Vault beneath Preferences, then confirm the Vault page is shown.
scenarios.expectedResult: Each entry opens its own page. Arrival must be judged on page content: Organization resolves to the same destination as the Dashboard Preferences icon, so an address-only assertion would pass without proving the right page was reached.
testDataRequirements: The configured Organization account, read only through env.requireEcoreLogin().

scenarios.title: Command Center returns the user to the Home page from each module
preconditions: An Organization user is signed in to eCore.
The user has navigated away from the Home page.
steps: From each module reached in this plan, select Command Center.
Confirm the Home page is displayed again before moving to the next module.
scenarios.expectedResult: Selecting Command Center returns the user to the Home page from every module. The return is confirmed after each module rather than once at the end, so a single failing module is identifiable.
testDataRequirements: The configured Organization account, read only through env.requireEcoreLogin().

scenarios.title: An unauthenticated visitor is refused a module and kept on the sign-in page
preconditions: A fresh browser session carrying no eCore sign-in.
No credentials are supplied at any point in this scenario.
steps: Request a module directly without signing in.
scenarios.expectedResult: An error message is shown and the sign-in page is still the page displayed. Two assertions only: that a message is present, and that the visitor has not been admitted. The wording of the message is not asserted in this version of the plan.
testDataRequirements: None. No credential is entered, so this scenario cannot contribute to an account lockout.

notes: eCore Command Center QA. The base URL and the organization credential are read only through src/utils/env.ts.
All seven scenarios are read-only navigation. Nothing in this plan creates, changes or deletes application data.
TS-ETA-411-007 needs a browser context with no stored session, so it must not reuse a signed-in state.

entryCriteria: Gate 1 is cleared: requirements/approved/ETA-411-ac-approval.json records an APPROVE decision for artifactVersion 1 of requirements/approved/ETA-411.json.
The approved OpenSpec change add-home-navigation validates strictly.
The configured account is signed in successfully at least once, proving the six modules are authorized for it.
exitCriteria: Every APPROVED acceptance criterion in ETA-411 is mapped to at least one scenario in this plan.
No DEFERRED acceptance criterion is mapped to any scenario, so REQ-ETA-411-001, REQ-ETA-411-006 and REQ-ETA-411-007 report as partially covered rather than met.
Each scenario has a real execution record; no result is recorded without one.
No scenario asserts a message string that has not been approved at this gate.
Arrival at Organization is asserted on page content, never on destination alone.

clarifications.question: Every scenario in this plan is declared interfaceType UI. That is a testing judgement rather than something ETA-411 states, and the workflow requires it to be put to you rather than decided silently. The basis: reports/validation/ETA-411-navigation-validation.json records all six destinations as full document requests to .eo pages, and reports/validation/ecore-api-discovery.json records that eCore has no REST resource model. Do you agree that no acceptance criterion in scope is API-verifiable this release?

TS-ETA-411-007 asserts that an error message is present, not what it says. The exact text will be captured at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION as OBSERVED. Asserting a captured string would make whatever eCore says today the definition of correct, so it needs your explicit approval in a later plan version. Do you accept the presence-only assertion for this version?

Organization in the navigation menu and the Preferences icon on the Dashboard both resolve to /ssweb/setup/prefs/preferences.eo. This plan treats that as the application's current shape and works around it by asserting on page content. Recorded so that if it is in fact a wiring defect, the plan is not the thing that hid it.

The Command Center control is a background-image div with no accessible name, so TS-ETA-411-006 will need a VALIDATED locator waiver. Whether the missing accessible name is itself a defect worth raising is a human judgement this plan does not make.

AC-ETA-411-002, AC-ETA-411-008 and AC-ETA-411-010 are DEFERRED and are deliberately not covered by any scenario here, so REQ-ETA-411-001, REQ-ETA-411-006 and REQ-ETA-411-007 will report as partially covered. Carried forward from AMB-ETA-411-002, -003 and -005.
